findings.evidence: The only matching declaration is `ofPath_mem_pathSpan` at lines 124–126, while the analogous arrow-ideal rule at lines 270–275 is a simp iff.
findings.fix: Add a `@[simp] theorem ofPath_mem_pathSpan_iff [Nontrivial k] : ofPath x ∈ pathSpan k Q n ↔ n ≤ x.2.2.length`.
findings.issue: `ofPath_mem_pathSpan` gives only the forward introduction rule; there is no iff characterizing when a basis path belongs to `pathSpan`, so consumers must unfold coordinates to eliminate such membership.

findings.evidence: A repository-wide grep finds no occurrence of an ideal power of `arrowIdeal`; lines 201–207 prove only `f ^ n ∈ pathSpan k Q n`, while roadmap lines 279–281 explicitly require `rad^n` and inclusions `rad^N ⊆ I ⊆ rad²`.
findings.fix: Package every filtration step as a two-sided ideal or add a theorem identifying its underlying submodule with `(arrowIdeal k Q)^n`.
findings.issue: The filtration is not related to ideal powers: `pow_mem_pathSpan` concerns powers of one element, but later radical-power and admissible-ideal consumers need the subobject equality between `pathSpan n` and `(arrowIdeal k Q)^n`.

summary: The prior findings are fixed, but the public length-filtration API still lacks its basis-path elimination rule and its key identification with powers of the arrow ideal.
